PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 27 years
Gestational Age at Sampling: 18 weeks
Indication for Testing: Prenatal screening for common aneuploidies

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Rapid aneuploidy screening for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniocytes extracted from amniotic fluid. DNA was amplified using fluorescently labeled primers for chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1414

Amplified products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis. Peak area ratios were calculated for informative markers to assess chromosome copy number.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: NORMAL
All informative markers showed normal biallelic patterns with peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome)

Chromosome 18: NORMAL
All informative markers showed normal biallelic patterns with peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
No evidence of trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome)

Chromosome 21: NORMAL
All informative markers showed normal biallelic patterns with peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
No evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome)

Sex Chromosome Markers: Consistent with female fetus (XX)

QUALITY METRICS
DNA concentration: Adequate
Amplification efficiency: >95% for all markers
Maternal cell contamination: Not detected

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis showed a normal chromosome complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No evidence of trisomy was detected for the tested chromosomes. This result significantly reduces but does not eliminate the risk of these common aneuploidies.

LIMITATIONS
QF-PCR is a targeted test that only assesses chromosomes 13, 18, 21, and sex chromosomes. This test does not detect:
- Other chromosome abnormalities
- Balanced rearrangements
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%)
- Single gene disorders
- Microdeletion/microduplication syndromes

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis of G-banded chromosomes from cultured amniocytes to follow. This comprehensive cytogenetic analysis will evaluate all chromosomes and can detect numerical and structural abnormalities not assessed by QF-PCR.

This report has been reviewed and electronically signed by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Prenatal Genetics Laboratory
[redacted date]
